facts.description: Binary is ELF64 x86-64 PIE executable, dynamically linked, not stripped, compiled with GCC 11.4.0
Security: Full RELRO, NX enabled, Canary, PIE, SHSTK+IBT (CET) enabled
No RPATH or RUNPATH in binary. Only NEEDED dependency is libc.so.6. LD_LIBRARY_PATH would take precedence over system paths.
main calls mmap(0x13370000, 0x64, PROT_READ|PROT_WRITE|PROT_EXEC=7, MAP_PRIVATE|MAP_ANONYMOUS=0x22, -1, 0) to allocate a 100-byte RWX region at fixed address 0x13370000
main reads up to 99 bytes (0x63) of user shellcode from stdin (fd 0) into the mmap buffer via read(0, buf, 0x63)

blacklist function iterates i=0..99 over the shellcode buffer and checks if any byte equals 0x0f. If found, returns 1 causing _abort with bye message. The byte 0x0f is the first byte of the x86-64 syscall instruction (0x0f 0x05).
After blacklist passes, main calls mprotect(buf, 0x64, 4) where 4=PROT_READ. This changes the mmap region from RWX to read-only (removes write and execute permissions).

Before jumping to shellcode, main clears ALL general-purpose registers (rax,rbx,rcx,rdx,rsi,rdi,r8-r15,rsp,rbp) and ALL XMM registers (xmm0-xmm15) to zero. Then sets rdi=0x13370000 and rbp=0, and executes jmp rdi to transfer control to the shellcode buffer.
The mmap buffer is at fixed address 0x13370000 (not ASLR-randomized). The shellcode region is 100 bytes (0x64).
init() sets stdin/stdout/stderr to unbuffered (_IONBF) and calls alarm(60) for a 60-second timeout.
probe_io with input AAAA (no 0x0f byte) resulted in Segmentation fault, consistent with mprotect making the region non-executable before jmp.
.rodata contains strings: percent-s, mmap failed, Input your shellcode here (max: 100), read failed, bye
GOT is in Full RELRO segment (GNU_RELRO covers 0x3d78-0x4000), made read-only at runtime. GOT overwrite not feasible at runtime.

The mprotect(buf, 0x64, PROT_READ=4) call removes execute permission from the shellcode buffer. Combined with NX enabled, the subsequent jmp rdi to 0x13370000 should trigger SIGSEGV. This appears to be a logic flaw: the intended behavior was likely mprotect(buf, 0x64, PROT_READ|PROT_EXEC=5) to allow execution while removing write permission.

The blacklist only blocks byte 0x0f. The syscall instruction is 0x0f 0x05. Since 0x0f is blocked, direct syscall cannot appear in shellcode. If the region were executable and writable, self-modifying code could bypass this, but mprotect removes both W and X, so self-modification is also blocked.

CET (IBT+SHSTK) is enabled via GNU_PROPERTY. IBT requires indirect branch targets to begin with endbr64. The jmp to 0x13370000 (user shellcode) would need the shellcode to start with endbr64 (f3 0f 1e fa) to satisfy IBT. Note: endbr64 contains byte 0x0f which is blacklisted.
